title: The One Mental Shift That Separates Good Content Teams From Great Ones
content:
Most content teams optimize for output. The best ones optimize for learning.

Output teams ask: how many posts did we publish this week?
Learning teams ask: what did we discover this week that changes what we publish next week?

The difference compounds. After six months, the learning team is operating on a fundamentally different plane. They know which messages resonate with which audience segments. They know which content types build pipeline and which ones just generate likes. They have eliminated an enormous amount of wasted effort.

The mental shift is simple but not easy: treat every piece of content as a hypothesis, not a deliverable.

A deliverable is done when it is published. A hypothesis is done when it has taught you something.

This reframe changes everything downstream — how you brief, how you measure, how you review, and how you decide what to build next.
target_audience_notes: Senior marketers and content leaders who engage with long-form LinkedIn articles. This audience skews toward sharing over commenting. Target through organic reach and sponsored distribution to lookalike audiences.

title: TechCorp: From 1.2% to 2.6% Engagement in 90 Days
content:
TechCorp's content team of 5 had a problem every content marketer recognizes.

Great ideas. No system. Engagement plateaued at 1.2% for six straight quarters.

They didn't hire more people. They changed their process.

Instead of writing new content from scratch for every campaign, they built a library of reusable content pieces — core messages, proof points, narrative hooks — that any team member could assemble into platform-specific posts.

Ninety days later:
↑ Engagement: 1.2% → 2.6%
↓ Production cycle: 14 days → 3 days
↑ Active platforms: 2 → 4
→ Team size: unchanged

"Within the first month we had reduced our content cycle from two weeks to three days." — Sarah Chen, Head of Content, TechCorp

The full case study is linked in comments.
target_audience_notes: Existing customers 30–90 days post-onboarding and warm prospects in active sales cycles. High-intent audience — this post should appear in sponsored distribution targeting users who have visited the pricing page.

title: Our API Takes 30 Minutes to Integrate. Here's Proof.
content:
Most "easy integration" claims fall apart when you actually try them.

So here's the exact sequence:

1. Generate an API key from Settings → Developer (30 seconds)
2. Send a GET to /api/campaigns with your Bearer token (2 minutes)
3. POST to /api/posts with campaign_id, platform_id, post type, and content (5 minutes)
4. Handle the 422 response body if validation fails — every error maps to a specific field with a plain-language message (10 minutes to read the docs)

That's it. You're publishing programmatically.

Rate limits: 1000 req/min. Headers included in every response. Exponential backoff on 429.

Full reference, SDKs in 7 languages, and a Postman collection are in the developer portal.

Link in comments. DMs open if you hit a wall.
target_audience_notes: Software engineers and technical leads evaluating the platform. LinkedIn engineering audience responds to specificity and step-by-step breakdowns over abstract capability claims.
